thread:
chris: ACME (tenant=acme-123) just filed an incident — ~40k audit events missing between 2026-03-16T02:00Z and 2026-03-16T08:00Z. Their SIEM shows gaps. I checked the export manifests; several shards are zero-byte and forwarder logs include `rate_limited=true` and `sampled_out=true` for the tenant. Pasting the manifest keys and a couple log lines below.

chris: S3 manifest snippet:
```
s3://audit-exports/2026/03/16/acme-123/shard-0001.manifest.gz
s3://audit-exports/2026/03/16/acme-123/shard-0002.manifest.gz
s3://audit-exports/2026/03/16/acme-123/shard-0003.manifest.gz  # zero-byte
```

chris: forwarder log (redacted):
```
2026-03-16T02:12:03Z forwarder[pid=211] tenant=acme-123 event_id=evt_7Hk2 rate_limited=true sampled_out=true sample_window=60s token_bucket=10/s burst=200
2026-03-16T02:12:03Z forwarder[pid=211] tenant=acme-123 event_id=evt_7Hk3 write_status=success s3_key=shard-0002/part-0001.gz
```

priya: thanks @chris — can you attach the full manifest for the window + 5 example event_ids and the forwarder config for acme-123? cc @raj (sre-oncall) and @security-ops.

chris: attaching (pasted inline due to sensitivity):
```
manifest: [shard-0001, shard-0002, shard-0003]
example_event_ids: [evt_7Hk2, evt_7Hk3, evt_8Lp9, evt_8LpA, evt_9Xy1]
forwarder config (tenant override): {
  route: SIEM-forwarder,
  sample: true,
  sample_window: 60,  # seconds
  rate_limit_per_tenant: 10,  # events/sec
  burst: 200
}
```

raj: quick read — looks like two things colliding: per-tenant token-bucket rate_limit=10/s with a 60s sampling window. Under short spikes the forwarder will drop (sampled_out) and you can also see zero-byte shards when a shard rotation happened but no events were written. This matches the customer's missing count.

priya: is this the sampling override we rolled out Q4? I thought tenant overrides were supposed to be disabled for SIEM-forwarder route. If overrides are applied, we might be sampling down critical audit events.

ellen: customer wants a replay + fixed ETA. Can we give them a safe playbook? They emphasized compliance/regulatory concerns.

raj: mitigation plan (short):
- step 1: temporarily bump acme-123 rate_limit to 1000/s and set sample=off for SIEM-forwarder (12h window)
- step 2: run a dry-run replay to verify manifests decrypt and map to SIEM schema
- step 3: schedule backfill (reencrypt + replay) for the missing window once dry-run OK

raj: repro commands and checks (for oncall):
```
# check forwarder live config for tenant
curl -H "X-Auth: $TOKEN" https://config.internal/tenants/acme-123/forwarder

# tail forwarder logs for flags
kubectl logs -l app=forwarder -c forwarder -n prod | grep acme-123 | tail -n 200

# verify manifest contents
aws s3 cp s3://audit-exports/2026/03/16/acme-123/shard-0002.manifest.gz - | zcat | head
```

chris: note — we also saw a transient KMS/HSM decrypt error earlier: `HSM: decrypt failed: nonce_mismatch` around 2026-03-16T02:05Z for a handful of shards. Not sure if alias rotated that night.

priya: do NOT run replay until security-ops confirms KMS alias/version. If an alias rotated and keys were retired, reencrypt will fail or produce garbage. @security-ops can you confirm alias state for acme-123?

security-ops: looking now. Confirmation: alias `alias/acme-123-audit` had a rotation 2026-03-16T01:58Z — new key active at 01:58Z, previous key scheduled for 30 days recovery. Decrypt failures likely from in-flight producers using old cached key references. No data lost on KMS side; reencrypt should be possible using the previous key ID as long as the old key material is still retained.

raj: good — that means replay path is viable. Playbook for replay (example):
```
# dry-run (non-destructive)
audit-replay --tenant acme-123 --from 2026-03-16T02:00Z --to 2026-03-16T08:00Z --dry-run --manifest s3://audit-exports/2026/03/16/acme-123/manifest.gz

# actual replay with reencrypt to current alias
audit-replay --tenant acme-123 --from 2026-03-16T02:00Z --to 2026-03-16T08:00Z --reencrypt --kms-alias alias/acme-123-audit --notify "support:acme-123"
```

ellen: customer asks for ETA. raj/ chris — how long to bump config and run dry-run?

chris: I can patch config to bump limits in ~20 mins, and dry-run will take ~2-3h to surface mapping issues at SIEM ingest rates. Full replay depends on event count; estimate 6-8h for the replay job once we confirm dry-run.

DevBot: Created ticket INF-5421: "acme-123 per-tenant sampling/rate-limit causing missing audit events; replay requested" — assigned to raj, priority P1.

priya: follow-ups:
- add a unit/e2e check that tenant overrides are ignored for SIEM-forwarder route
- run an eval on sampling semantics to ensure sample_window isn't applied at shard-level unexpectedly

raj: I'll open a PR for the config change (patch + rollback) and attach the replay job logs here after dry-run.

ellen: I'll update the customer with this plan + ETA (dry-run ~3h, full replay ~6-8h after). Will mention KMS check complete.

chris: starting config patch now, will DM if anything blocks. :thumbsup:

security-ops: if replay hits any KMS HSM nonce errors, stop and notify us immediately. We'll escalate to HSM vendor.

raj: ack. attaching quick checklist for whoever runs the replay:
- confirm alias key IDs w/ security-ops
- run dry-run and verify ~100 sample events in SIEM mapping
- if mapping ok, run full replay with rate limit throttle to avoid SIEM overload
- mark job in INF-5421 and set watchers

chris: thanks team. I’ll post logs and manifest copies to the ticket when dry-run finishes.
